Part 2 · TE-1 stage by stage

How does a finished case look?

Part 2 · the plan

One real run of TE-1, followed through

Open it yourself: Worked examples ▸ TE-1 ▸ Open example.

  1. Stage 0 to Definesymptom with numbers, the physics, the problem statement
  2. Explorefishbone, seven hypotheses, each with a falsifier
  3. Plan and Do itS/D/N screen, three tests, the fix and its check
  4. Look backthe barrier and the cost ledger

Stage 0 · the problem

“Ethylene loss up, TIC-107 on set point”

Situation given

The group runs TE-1 for 30 min of OTS time and touches nothing. Then it writes what was seen, by whom and when.

Stage 0 · trends · interactive

Thirty minutes on the DCS

AI-114 and the loss climb while TI-107 stays near −97 °C; the kettle level and FI-304 fall.

Review R and Engage 1

Write the physics, then judge the urgency

\(y_{C_2H_4} = K(T,P)\,x_{C_2H_4}\)
  • At fixed PIC-112, colder V-102 gas means less ethylene lost.
  • TIC-107 moves the LIC-108 set point: level sets the E-102 duty.
  • Engage 1.4: keep running and investigate; no limit is near.

Define 2 · IS / IS NOT

Where the problem is, and where it is not

Explore 3.4 · cause and effect

Every idea on a bone first

Each bone idea becomes one working hypothesis on 3.6.

Explore 3.6 · working hypotheses

“If … then we should observe …”

  • Seven hypotheses, one per cause.
  • Each states what we should see and what would kill it.
  • A hypothesis without a falsifier cannot be tested.

Plan 4.3 · S / D / N · interactive

Screen the hypotheses with the evidence you own

Evidence lines (tap to switch off)

One firm D drops a hypothesis; count the S only among the survivors.

Plan 4.6 · the plant-test plan

Three tests, cheapest first, written before any move

Do it 5.0 · T-2 desk check

What temperature does AI-114 say the drum is at?

\(y_{C_2H_4} = K(T,P)\,x_{C_2H_4}\)

Flash the V-101 vapour at PI-112 and find the T that gives the AI-114 reading.

The drum gas is about 4 °C warmer than TI-107 says. Feed and pressure are cleared.

Do it 5.0 · T-3 on the OTS · interactive

TIC-107 set point −97 → −99 °C: does AI-114 follow?

AI-114 fell with the level rising, as WH-1 predicted: the controller works; its reading is low. WH-3 killed.

Do it 5.5–5.6 · fix and verify · interactive

Offset now, recalibrate, then check the prediction

  • 0:46 SP −101 °C: a temporary 4 °C offset.
  • 1:06 TT-107 recalibrated; SP back to −97 °C.
  • 1:26 AI-114 2.21 mol%, loss 295 kg/h.

Predicted before the fix: AI-114 ≈ 2.12 mol%, loss ≈ 283 kg/h. The run ends close to both.

Look back 6.4 · cost ledger · interactive

Was the troubleshooting worth it?

\(\text{value} = \Delta\dot m \cdot t \cdot \text{price},\ \Delta\dot m = 86\ \text{kg/h}\)

Prices are the OTS teaching values (ethylene USD 1 000/t, fuel USD 300/t); the method is the point.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • Numbers and times first; TI-107 sat on set point while AI-114 rose.
  • Seven hypotheses with falsifiers; lab and desk check killed five.
  • One set-point move proved TT-107 reads low; the fix was checked.

Rules for the graded cases

TE-1 is the model; TE-2 … TE-12 are yours

StepThe group does
Loadthe case in Exercises and the same case on Case & team
Run15–30 min of OTS time without touching anything
Recordpull all three; keep facts apart from opinions
Testwrite the plan, then make the one move
Hand in.woods.json, the report and the slides

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • The readiness check shows what is still empty.
  • Report and slides come from the record, not from memory.
  • The .woods.json file is the hand-in.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Write the symptom with numbers, tags and times before any cause.

2

Check one instrument against the physics of another.

3

Screen with the evidence you own before you move anything.

4

Write the test plan first: one move, predictions, stop rule, way back.

5

Verify the fix against its prediction, then close the ledger.
